study type: Retrospective observational study utilising machine learning for prediction
exposure: Clinical variables (e.g., last recorded postoperative pain score, mean and standard deviation of hourly maximum postoperative pain score)
outcome: Significant postoperative pain (maximum pain score of 3 or more on movement at 13th to 24th hour post-spinal morphine)
cohort: The study cohort comprised 6561 women who underwent caesarean delivery and received postoperative spinal morphine in a single specialist maternity hospital.
finding: Ridge regression demonstrated the best performance (AUC: 0.719) among six modeling techniques in predicting significant postoperative pain after caesarean delivery.
followup_time: 13 to 24 hours after spinal morphine administration
